trigger: an apt source URI whose password contains a raw '?' or '#'
summary: redact_url_userinfo ended the authority at '/ ? # whitespace'; apt ends it only at '/'. Fixed in 0117b284b (per-field placement + terminator fix).

trigger: apt-legal source-list shapes: whitespace-only line between deb822 stanzas, hidden/odd sources.list.d file names, bracket-grouped cdrom URIs, yum-vocabulary trust tokens
summary: Plugin's one-line/deb822 parsing disagreed with real apt (2.0-3.2, verified in containers) on several shapes, each producing a wrong-but-labelled-correct row. Fixed in 4608147b2.

trigger: an in-place truncate+write rewriter racing read_file's fstat/read/fstat window
summary: fstat-then-read was not atomic against an in-place writer; a shrink-to-zero read reported supported+zero rows. Fixed in 4608147b2 with a two-fstat stamp compare plus a just_emptied guard; residual (a file kept empty for the whole read window) is inherent and documented.

trigger: a NUL or non-UTF-8 byte inside a surfaced apt_source field
summary: A NUL cut a row at the host strlen boundary (trust columns lost while status still said supported); invalid UTF-8 made the whole CommandResponse unparseable, tearing down the agent's Subscribe stream. adversarial-review r1 had deferred this as a systemic shared-boundary issue; Gate 4 evidence changed the calculus and it was fixed in-branch in 4608147b2 via scrub_wire_bytes. The shared SDK-level fix for other plugins is issue #4864 (filed, not this branch's job).

trigger: any CI run of the capability-matrix drift gate (Linux leg) on this branch
summary: Generated matrix rows / README fence / plugin JSON said 'follows as its own PR' while the compiled descriptor said 'not read yet'. Regenerated from the built dylib (host-independent descriptor, no #if) in afa3ea7f0.

policy_floor: manual resource cleanup in new C++ not RAII-wrapped
summary: New raw ::open/::close in test code, not RAII, absent from the Gate 1 ledger. Fixed with ScopedFd in afa3ea7f0's round.

trigger: a '%' anywhere inside an option block, including an option this plugin ignores
summary: Round-2's new refuse rule was broader than apt: apt accepts a %-encoded option value. The whole entry was dropped, hiding a real, apt-used source. Fixed in 0e396626f by removing the blanket refusal and decoding a surfaced option's own value instead.

trigger: a double quote anywhere in a one-line entry
summary: apt de-quotes a quoted option value or word; the plugin's blanket quote refusal dropped real sources apt reads (e.g. [signed-by="/a b.gpg"]). Fixed in 0e396626f: quotes are stripped from a surfaced option's value via a new quote-aware option splitter (split_apt_options); a quoted whole URI/type/suite word is accepted but not re-tokenised (documented residual, narrow).

trigger: a deb822 or one-line URI whose password contains a %XX-encoded slash before the real '@' (e.g. URIs: http://bob:%2fSEKR3T@host/apt, which apt resolves keeping %2f literal)
summary: Round-2's redaction fix decoded the whole word BEFORE locating the authority boundary, so a %2f in the password decoded to a literal '/' and stopped the authority scan short, missing the '@' entirely and returning the credential fully unredacted -- a fresh instance of the exact class sec-1 first found. Fixed in 0e396626f: the split now runs on raw bytes only (matching apt's own observed behaviour), with %3a/%3A recognised only as an alternate SCHEME separator. Verified against real apt and with a targeted mutation (restoring decode-before-split fails the test suite).

trigger: a Linux host whose update sources are zypper, pacman or apk (not apt or rpm/dnf)
summary: Already ruled a documented scope limit at the first code-review round (G20); the plugin now states the limit on every wire-visible surface (descriptor note, action description, definition, README) rather than only a README caveat, per ent-1/con-1. Whether to add tripwires for these families, as the rpm tripwire does, is a scope/product decision for Alex -- not implemented this round.
adjudicated_by: code-review Architect ruling G19/G20 (2026-09-21), reaffirmed by this governance run
adjudication_rationale: Facts derive HIGH (I3/E3) mechanically. Already ruled a documented, in-scope decision at the first code-review gate (G19: 'for_alex, recommended: document as is') rather than a defect: the plugin's roadmap row charters apt + rpm/dnf only, and the limit is now stated on every wire-visible surface. Whether to add tripwires for zypper/pacman/apk (matching the rpm tripwire pattern) is Alex's scope call, tracked at issue #4871; not implemented this round.

trigger: one malformed or unrecognised apt entry anywhere on the host (any file under sources.list.d, either format)
summary: Verified against real apt 3.0.3: a single malformed entry in one file makes apt refuse ALL sources host-wide ('E: The list of sources could not be read'), including a completely separate, well-formed file. The plugin's per-entry model still emits full apt_source rows for the well-formed entries, asserting trust facts for sources apt is not actually using at all. This mechanically derives HIGH (I3/E3) but reworking the reporting model (per-entry vs apt's all-or-nothing) is a design decision, not a mechanical bug fix; not implemented this round per the operator's standing instruction to flag rather than silently pick a design direction.
adjudicated_by: orchestrator (gate-8 second re-review), per the operator's standing instruction to flag design decisions rather than silently pick one
adjudication_rationale: Facts derive HIGH (I3/E3) mechanically, but the fix is a reporting-model redesign (per-entry vs apt's all-or-nothing validation), not a mechanical bug fix; filed as issue #4878 with full context rather than implemented, and flagged prominently in the final report to Alex rather than deferred silently.

trigger: a NUL or non-UTF-8 byte inside a URI's userinfo portion, which redact_url_userinfo strips before scrubbing runs
summary: apt_rows_from_text's altered accounting is derived from the RAW fact text before url_field's redaction step, so a bad byte that gets redacted away (never reaches the wire) still flips the result to constrained/invalid_bytes -- contradicting the round's own doc claim ('a byte that REACHES a reported field'). Row content is correct and safe either way (I8, not I1/I3); deferred to a follow-up issue rather than fixed in-branch given branch size.

trigger: the macOS, Windows and rpm/dnf legs deferred by the size split existing only on a local, unpushed wip branch with no issue or roadmap row
summary: Three full-context issues filed (#4868 macOS, #4869 Windows, #4870 rpm/dnf) before the push gate, closing this.

Sibling app_control plugin has a routed-concern row; this plugin does not. Not a required doc under rule 4 (no new catastrophic invariant); recommended as a decision for Alex at rebase/push time, not actioned this gate round.
